messages.author: ad0ee449d01ce080
messages.subject: Adjusting 'NA' points in gl.pcoa.plot output
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use the argument 'as.pop=' to display various features on my PCoA plot, e.g. discrete phenotypes or population groupings based on geography. In most cases these alternative population datasets contain missing data, which I have coded as 'NA' in the metadata file. 

When these are plotted using gl.pcoa.plot() the 'NA' values appear gray, which is good; however, the problem is that the NA values are plotted on top of everything else. For example, I plotted observations of flavor onto my original PCoA using gl.pcoa.plot(x_pca, x, as.pop="flavor", xaxis=1, yaxis=2). The attached screenshot shows a portion of the resulting plot.

Based on the placement of the label it is possible to infer where the "bitter" flavors are clustering, yet the majority of observations are hidden behind the gray 'NA' points. Is there a way to plot the actual data on top of the NA points, or to increase the opacity of the 'NA' points (alpha=0.5?) so that the actual data can still be viewed? 

Thanks,
David

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Adjusting 'NA' points in gl.pcoa.plot output
parts:
Hi David, 

You can try this approach:

#installing developing version of dartR
library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
library(dartR)
t1 <- your_dataset
pcoa<- gl.pcoa(t1)
res <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa,t1)
res + geom_point(color ="white",size=3 ) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(alpha = ifelse(is.na(pop(t1)), 0, 1))

Cheers,
Luis

messages.author: d87216285ace7535
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: Adjusting 'NA' points in gl.pcoa.plot output
parts:
G'day David

From your emails it is not clear why you are including individuals
listed as NA, because they have missing data in a pcoa plot. PCoA does
not like missing data as it fills in missing values with the overall
average for the dataset. You should be removing individuals with excess
missing data.

PCoA is usually done in a step wise manner, going from the broader
scales to finer scales to reveal patterns in your data. First step
might be your ingroup, or a specific clade (based on a phylogeny), then
you remove the most obvious outliers and run it again until you get to a
point where it's no longer informative for the populations included.

If you are trying to compare different portions of your dataset then you
need to exclude those individuals that you aren't trying to compare.
This can be done using an index command. The ! means does not, if you
wanted to only select a certain population or combination of populations
then change the ! to =

index <- gl@other$ind.metrics$pop !="NA"
gl <- gl[ index, ]

This example includes only two pops and removes all others.

index <- gl@other$ind.metrics$pop =="pop_name1" |
gl@other$ind.metrics$pop =="pop_name2"
gl <- gl[ index, ]

Alternatively you can use the following commands to do a similar thing.

gl <- gl.drop.pop(gl, pop.list=c('pop_name1'))
gl <- gl.drop.pop(gl, pop.list=c('pop_name1','pop_name2'))

You can substitute drop for keep too.

Cheers
Peter

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: Adjusting 'NA' points in gl.pcoa.plot output
parts:
Hi Luis,

The solution was very close to your original suggestion. Rather than calling pop from the genlight object, I called it from res and it worked as intended.

#installing developing version of dartR
library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
library(dartR)

t1 <- your_genlight
pcoa<- gl.pcoa(t1)
#Set the transparency parameter
alpha_val <- 0.05
# Pass PCoA plot to res
res <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa, t1, as.pop = "flavor")

res + geom_point(color = "white")+
  theme_bw()+

geom_point(alpha = ifelse(is.na(res$data$pop), alpha_val,1))


Thanks again for your help with this!
David

Hi Luis,

 

The solution was very close to your original suggestion. Rather than calling pop from the genlight object, I called it from res and it worked as intended.

 

#installing developing version of dartR
library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
library(dartR)
t1 <- your_genlight
pcoa<- gl.pcoa(t1)

#Set the transparency parameter

alpha_val <- 0.05

# Pass PCoA plot to res

res <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa, t1, as.pop = "flavor")

res + geom_point(color = "white")+
  theme_bw()+
  geom_point(alpha = ifelse(is.na(res$data$pop), alpha_val,1))

Thanks again for your help with this!

David

You make a good point Bernd! I've made some adjustments below. It's not perfect as the legend does not respond to changes in alpha_val, but I think it's a better match. Thanks for the suggestion!

#install developing version of dartR, load genlight, run pcoa

library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
library(dartR)

t1 <- your_genlight
pcoa<- gl.pcoa(t1)

# Pass PCoA plot to res, add custom colors
col_flav<-c("#3C3CE6", "#9654C2", "#C42D2D")
res <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa, t1, as.pop = "flavor", pt.colors = col_flav)

#Set the transparency parameter
alpha_val <- 0.05
#Change theme, add transparency to NA points, modify legend NA point, add legend title

res + geom_point(color = "white")+
  theme_bw()+

geom_point(alpha = ifelse(is.na(res$data$pop), alpha_val,1))+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = ifelse(is.na(unique(res$data$pop, fromLast = T)), 21, 19))))+
  labs(color = "Flavor")



Best,
David

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: Adjusting 'NA' points in gl.pcoa.plot output
parts:
Please disregard my previous message. I found a solution elsewhere on the forum. Pasting here for anyone looking to use this method for plot modifications in the future. Keylines highlighted in yellow. The rest are just custom options I've selected for my plot.

#Load genlight and run PCoA

t1 <- your_dataset
pcoa<- gl.pcoa(t1)

#PCA plot with save2tmp=TRUE
gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa, t1, as.pop = "groove", pt.colors = col_groove, xaxis = 1, yaxis = 2, save2tmp = TRUE)

#listing the plots in tempdir
gl.list.reports()

#choose the plot to retrieve
res <- gl.print.reports(1)

#Set the transparency parameter
alpha_val <- 0.05

#choose colors
col_groove<-c("#AFE5B3", "#2D3A7C")

#Customize plot options
res + geom_point(color = "white")+
theme_classic()+

geom_point(alpha = ifelse(is.na(res$data$pop), alpha_val,1))+
